newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks end weaker, await MSCI changes.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks end weaker, await MSCI changes.

text.p: Singapore shares ended soft on Friday after trading defensively amid speculation that Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) had plans to re-weight regional stocks markets, including Singapore, dealers said.
MSCI earlier rated the equity market here the worst performer in Asia for March, below Hong Kong and Malaysia.
"It looks like a re-allocation of weighting for all markets across the board. This market found that a good reason to stay spooked," a dealer with a U.S. brokerage said.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) clawed back to 2,019.60 points, down a modest 0.57, on short covering.
Intraday the index fell to two-year lows at 2,007.47 points, but liquidity was thin with volume at 102 million shares.
Dealers said they expect the market to be plagued by more institutional selling next week, especially foreign tranches of blue chip stocks, if Singapore is re-weighted by MSCI.
A lack of arbitrage opportunities against Malaysian issues was also blamed for lacklustre over-the-counter trade.
Index-linked Keppel Corp ended Singapore 25 cents lower at S$6.55, and SingTel dropped three cents to S$2.51. SIA foreign attracted better demand, up 40 cents to $12.70, on fundamentals.
